answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Consistency Rule. Each identity must repeat a minimum set of prior-epoch interaction partners; new partners per epoch are capped. An agent on a small island of activity cannot suddenly connect to the whole ocean of the network without penalty. Legitimate identities accumulate a stable harbor of recurring counterparties over time. An attacker must sustain many identities across epochs, paying the full per-identity cost of repeated interactions and history maintenance rather than a one-time fee, making each fake identity linearly costly to keep alive.
